Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is the security questionnaire we include with our RFPs. Two items are particularly important for Nutexa: (1) detailed network zoning and egress controls for multi-tenant inference, and (2) how you mitigate supply‑chain/injection attacks that might originate from third-party runtime components or model artifacts.

Can you provide a technical narrative and annotated diagram for:
- Tenant isolation across control plane, compute, and storage
- Egress control points and encryption in flight at each boundary
- Patch and artifact provenance controls (how you validate models/kernels before deployment)
- Incident playbook for suspected vendor-supplied compromise (containment, rollback, forensic artifacts)

We'd like a single PDF bundle by EOD Wednesday. Attaching the questionnaire and a simple template.

Attachments: Nutexa_RFP_Q3_Security_Appendix.pdf (questionnaire)

Jordan —

Draft attached: I focused the narrative around three zones (Control Plane, Tenant Compute, Persistent Storage) and called out explicit egress choke points (egress gateway, NAT per AZ, sidecar egress policy). I also added a small appendix describing how we implement per-tenant network policies using our sidecar + VPC isolation for Private deployments.

Key bullets:
- Control Plane: Authenticated API endpoints > management plane segregated in a customer-managed VPC for Private deployments or dedicated control cluster for Dedicated customers.
- Tenant Compute: Strict process isolation via container sandboxes, per-tenant kernel build pins, and continuous runtime attestation. KV cache is scoped per tenant and never persisted to shared storage.
- Persistent Storage: Per-tenant encrypted object stores; key separation via KMS namespaces.

I attached an annotated diagram (redwood-zone-diagram-v2.png) and a short supply-chain lifecycle doc summarizing signing and provenance.

Attachments: redwood-zone-diagram-v2.png; supply-chain-threat-lifecycle.docx

LMK if you want edits before I merge with Karthik/Vanessa text.

Lauren/Jordan —

Adding the technical detail on artifact validation:
- All model artifacts and runtime kernels that enter our serving fleet must be signed via our internal artifact registry. We use a PKI-backed signing service (root managed by Redwood; customer-managed root available for Private deployments).
- At deployment time, the serving agent verifies the signature and checks the artifact hash against a provenance ledger (immutable entry in our internal ledger service that records builder id, build-time deps, and CVE-scanned SBOM).
- Kernel/ops patching: we stage patches in a canary pool; automated smoke-tests include adversarial prompt-timeouts and performance regression checks. If canaries fail, rollback is automatic via the orchestration state store (typical recovery 5–15 minutes depending on model size).
- Third-party models: we require a signed SBOM and run a lightweight static analysis and model-behavioral-fuzzing run before allowing them into Dedicated or Private pools. For Hosted API tier we offer curated/verified model catalog only.

I've added this text into the draft doc (inline). I also included a sample playbook for suspected supply-chain compromise: isolate pool, snapshot KV and ephemeral state, mark artifacts deprecated in registry, and trigger forensic snapshot (immutable logs + container image hashes).

— Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Asha / Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask and the template. Attached is our response bundle: a 3‑page narrative that maps to your questionnaire, an annotated topology diagram that highlights control plane / tenant compute / storage boundaries, and a short supply-chain lifecycle write-up that describes artifact signing, provenance ledger, and rollback/playbook steps. Highlights:
- Per‑tenant network isolation via sidecar + VPC pairs for Private deployments; dedicated GPU pools for Dedicated customers.
- Egress choke points implemented at per-AZ NAT + egress gateway; default-deny egress policy with allowlists per customer routes.
- Artifact provenance: PKI-signed artifacts, immutable provenance ledger entries, SBOM + fuzz-testing for third-party models.
- Incident playbook: immediate isolation, rollback to last-known-good artifact, forensic snapshot and chain-of-custody logs.

Attachments: RFP_Response_Package.pdf (compiled narrative + diagram + proofs) — also uploaded to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/DEAL-8342/RFP_Response_Package

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the level of detail. The diagram and provenance description address most of our concerns. Two follow-ups before we close this section:
1) For Private deployments with a customer-managed PKI root, can you provide the precise rotation cadence you support and the procedure for key compromise?
2) In your incident playbook, do you capture transient prompt inputs and KV cache snapshots for forensic analysis, and if so, how long are those retained and under what legal controls?

If you can answer those in a short note, we can mark the questionnaire as complete. Otherwise we'd like the 30m walkthrough.

Thanks — Asha
